items.check: The fingerprint comparison call is a real pyacoustid API, and a failure to compare is counted rather than returned as similarity 0.0
items.note: Re-verified against CC-M-005-001/002 v3 in plan.json: _similarity now returns Optional[float] and returns None (not 0.0) on any decode/compare failure, incrementing stats['fingerprint_compare_errors'] first. Both call sites now explicitly guard on None before treating the value as a real similarity score: _cluster_candidates unions only 'if similarity is not None and similarity > MATCH_THRESHOLD', and fingerprint_key_provider's provide() does 'if similarity is None: continue' before the MATCH_THRESHOLD/NEAR_MATCH_THRESHOLD branches. A compare failure can therefore no longer be mistaken for a genuine zero-similarity result at any matching decision point. acoustid.compare_fingerprints(a,b) remains a real pyacoustid API (confirmed previously). Check passes.

The prior FAIL note described a raw-text search on record.file_name that no longer exists in the diffs: both files only entry-lookup mechanism is element_span_by_identity(source_text, root, record.entry) (spans.py, CC-M-006-001), which locates a span by the elements tree position among same-tag elements in document order, not by searching source text for any attribute value. spans.py own docstring explicitly states this is chosen specifically to avoid breaking on duplicate FILE basenames and XML-escaped characters. split.py build_output (CC-M-008-002) additionally carries an inline comment stating the same rationale, and wraps the element_span_by_identity call in try/except ValueError, returning a SplitOutcome error rather than raising uncaught. items.finding: CI-M-006-002 was re-worded to describe add_counted_span as a generic opt-in per-container primitive ("a caller opts into for any container it rebuilds - COLLECTION ENTRIES and the root SUBNODES COUNT in splice.py, and PLAYLIST ENTRIES and SUBNODES COUNT in split.py"), correcting the prior overclaim that OutputBuilder itself recalculates every playlist count. The splice.py half of this new claim checks out: CC-M-007-002 assemble_output calls builder.add_counted_span(...) for COLLECTION/ENTRIES and for the root SUBNODES/COUNT. But the split.py half is still inaccurate: split.py never imports or calls OutputBuilder or add_counted_span at all (CC-M-008-001/002 import only element_span_by_identity, find_element_span, recalculate_count_attr from .spans - no OutputBuilder). build_output recalculates COLLECTION ENTRIES and the root SUBNODES COUNT via a local free function _replace_children(), which calls recalculate_count_attr() directly and manually finds/replaces the tag body by string slicing - not via OutputBuilder.add_counted_span. And PLAYLIST ENTRIES on a partially-kept playlist is recalculated by a third, different mechanism again: a cloned ElementTree node has entries removed in-place and playlist_elem.attrib["ENTRIES"] = str(len(surviving)) is set directly, then re-serialised with ET.tostring() - no string-level count-attr rewrite and no OutputBuilder involvement at all. So the corrected code_intent still misdescribes split.py: it claims split.py's PLAYLIST ENTRIES/SUBNODES COUNT recalculation goes through the add_counted_span primitive, but split.py recalculates those counts through two other, unrelated code paths (recalculate_count_attr via _replace_children, and direct ElementTree attribute assignment) and does not use OutputBuilder at all. The code itself (both mechanisms) is internally consistent and correct for what it does; the mismatch is that the intent narrative names the wrong primitive as the one split.py uses.

items.check: Identity grouping applies the record_keys tier cascade rather than only the single highest-confidence key
Per-tier matched_* counters agree with the final matched total after destination collisions are withdrawn
items.note: Fixed: resolve_reconnection now re-derives the winning tier for each withdrawn collision by finding the first key_name in record_keys() order whose indexes bucket equals [winner], and decrements matched_<tier> for it before setting stats['matched'] = len(final_mapping). Since match_records selects matched_by as the first tier with a length-1 bucket (same indexes object, same record_keys order), the re-derivation is guaranteed to find and decrement exactly the same tier match_records credited, for every collided key. Sum(matched_<tier>) after decrement = original sum - collided_count = original matched - collided_count = final matched. Invariant holds.
